references.text: Lamentations describes a similar desperate hunger: 'Those who died by the sword were better off than those who died of starvation' (Klag 4:9). The prodigal son's hunger was so great that he wished to fill his stomach with pig food, an image of the deepest degradation.

Amos prophesies about hunger as God's judgment: 'I gave you empty stomachs in all your towns' (Am 4:6-8). The prodigal son's hunger reflects a state of spiritual and physical distress resulting from turning away.
Proverbs warns that 'the drunkard and the glutton will come to poverty' (Ordsp 23:21). The prodigal son had squandered his inheritance in a dissolute life and was now experiencing the consequences.

Isaiah describes one who 'lives on ashes' and is deceived by their own heart (Jes 44:20). The prodigal son was in a similar state of self-deception and humiliation, as he tried to satisfy himself with food meant for pigs.

The context of the story: After using up all his possessions, a famine came, he began to suffer need, and ended up feeding pigs (Luk 15:14-15). Verse 16 elaborates on the depth of his degradation – that no one even gave him anything.

The prodigal son's realization follows directly after his desperate state: 'Then he came to himself' (Luk 15:17). The hunger and degradation in verse 16 were the turning point that drove him to repentance.

In the parable of the rich man and Lazarus, Lazarus wished 'to be filled with what fell from the rich man's table' (Luk 16:21). The same Greek expression (ἐπεθύμει) is used for a desperate and unfulfilled desire for food – a clear parallel to the prodigal son's situation.

The psalmist says: 'I was foolish and without understanding, I was like a beast before you' (Sal 73:22). The prodigal son had been reduced to an animal level, as he envied the pigs their food – a powerful image of sin's degradation.

The Lord's promise through Jeremiah: 'I will satisfy the weary soul and fill every fainting soul' (Jer 31:25). This contrast emphasizes that God can fill the hungry – something the prodigal son experienced when he returned to his father.
